headline: Wisconsin Inmates Become Conservation Heroes Raising Monarch Butterflies
meta_description: Inmates at Redgranite Correctional Institute raise and tag monarch caterpillars to help reverse declining butterfly populations across Wisconsin.
summary_short: Wisconsin prison inmates are raising monarch caterpillars in a conservation program, helping reverse population decline while giving back to their community.
body:
At Redgranite Correctional Institute in Wisconsin, an unlikely group of conservationists is working to save the monarch butterfly. Some 20 prisoners now participate in the Refuge for Growth, Change and Inspiration Monarch Program, which launched in 2025, tending to caterpillars in a purpose-built lepidopterum within the prison grounds. Over the June-to-September season, participants change leaves, collect data on eggs, and tag butterflies preparing for their thousand-mile migration to Mexico. The program has grown remarkably: this year it oversaw 100 caterpillars, up from 60 in its inaugural year. For inmates like Nathan Lecker, the work connects to childhood memories and offers something deeper than routine—a genuine contribution to conservation from inside prison walls.

The program emerged from an elegant idea: program organizer Carrie Jahnke sought meaningful work for prisoners unable to participate in sports. What began as an accommodation has proven profoundly popular, offering delicate, purposeful labor that inmates find fulfilling. Educational materials about monarchs, pollinator plants, and horticulture accompany the hands-on work, transforming the daily routine into active learning. Once butterflies emerge from their chrysalises, they need only 2 to 3 days to build strength before release.

Support has extended beyond the lepidopterum itself. Prison landscapers have planted monarch-friendly flower beds around the facility grounds, creating a supportive ecosystem as the insects depart. The Natural Resources Foundation of Wisconsin helped build the structure, recognizing both the ecological value and the human potential. As Shelly Torkelson, the foundation's communications director, noted, monarch populations have declined for years—making this partnership between incarceration and conservation a meaningful response to a genuine conservation crisis.
quick_facts: 20 Wisconsin prison inmates raise monarchs at Redgranite Correctional Institute
Program grew from 60 caterpillars in year one to 100 in year two
Inmates tag butterflies for 1,000-mile migration to Mexico
Launched in 2025, runs June through September each year
